newsitem.title: USA: Sears December same store sales up.
newsitem.headline: Sears December same store sales up.

text.p: Sears, Roebuck and Co said Thursday that its domestic same store sales for the five weeks ended January 4 rose 9.5 percent.
That increase compared with a 6.8 percent rise in same-store sales a year ago.
Total domesic store sales for the five-week period gained 14.6 percent to $4.28 billion, compared with $3.74 billion for the five weeks ended January 6, 1996.
For the 48 weeks ending January 4, Sears reported total revenues of $35.42 billion, up from the $32.50 billion in the same period of 1995.
Comparable store sales for that period were up 6.1 percent, Sears said.

"We experienced record sales in December, including our first-ever back-to-back billion-dollar sales weeks," Arthur Martinez, chairman, said in a statement. "The outstanding performance of our full-line stores was led by double-digit increases in all our softline categories -- women's, men's and children's apparel, shoes, accessories, cosmetics, fine jewelry and home fashions -- and in computers, electronics, tools and hardware on the hardline side."
